findings.description: The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so the database storage, snapshots and automated backups are stored unencrypted, and no KMS customer-managed key is specified. Any access to the underlying storage or a shared snapshot exposes the data in clear text.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the MySQL instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, exposing the database to internet-wide scanning and brute-force attacks. A database tier should reside in private subnets with no public addressing.

The master user is the default name 'admin', which removes the need for an attacker to guess a username and makes credential-stuffing/brute-force attempts against the publicly reachable endpoint significantly easier.

The master password is supplied through var.password and is stored in Terraform state in plain text and reused inline in EC2 user data; no secrets manager reference or managed master password is used, and lifecycle ignore_changes on password prevents rotation through code.

No enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports (audit, error, general, slowquery) are configured, so authentication and query activity against this internet-exposed database is not retained for security investigation.
iam_database_authentication_enabled is not set, so the database relies solely on a long-lived static master password rather than short-lived IAM-issued credentials.

The MySQL 8.0 parameter group sets only character-set parameters and does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so the database accepts unencrypted client connections and credentials/query data can be intercepted on the network.

The DB subnet group is built from aws_subnet.web_subnet and web_subnet2 — the same web-tier subnets used by the public instance — so the database is not isolated in a private network layer, which combined with publicly_accessible = true yields a directly reachable database.
The RDS security group allows all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data-exfiltration and command-and-control path from the database tier.

The EC2 instance role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", allowing the web instance to read/delete any bucket, launch or terminate any instance, and modify any database in the account — a privilege escalation and data exfiltration path if the web application is compromised.

The instance user_data embeds the database endpoint, username and var.password in clear text; user data is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute and via the instance metadata service, leaking the DB master credentials.

No metadata_options block enforces http_tokens = "required", so the legacy unauthenticated instance metadata service remains available; an SSRF in the PHP application becomes theft of the highly privileged instance-profile credentials.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance volume (which stores the credentials written into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc) may be created unencrypted.
